request: Add a --once flag to cmd/poller for immediate single-cycle collection, hitting the real CollectAll path and persisting data, without duplicating collection logic. Export logCycle as LogCycle so both paths share one report formatter.

tasks.title: Export logCycle → LogCycle in internal/telemetry/scheduler.go
tasks.notes: renamed logCycle -> LogCycle (signature + body unchanged), updated single call site in Scheduler.Run, refreshed doc comment to note export for shared formatter with cmd/poller --once. go vet ./internal/telemetry/... clean, telemetry tests pass.

tasks.title: Add --once flag to cmd/poller/main.go and branch on *once
tasks.notes: added 'flag' import, flag.Bool('once')+flag.Parse before config.Load, moved time.LoadLocation block inside if !*once, kept signal.NotifyContext + pool/acct/tcfg/collector construction once before the branch, added else CollectAll->LogCycle->log.Fatalf on whole-cycle error. Package doc comment updated with --once usage line. go vet ./cmd/poller ./internal/telemetry/... clean, gofmt clean. Guard is !*once (once is *bool) per design D4.

review.brief: Review telemetry-add-poller-once-flag: (1) module-boundary compliance — telemetry gains no new imports, cmd/poller adds only stdlib flag; (2) doc-pack conventions — go-conventions (cmd/ thin, no business logic), architecture (interface-first, no cross-module DB), telemetry AGENTS.md (no HTML, no config import); (3) spec/tasks coverage — tasks.md sub-tasks match what was implemented, spec GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios match behavior; (4) design compliance — D1 (export LogCycle, shared formatter), D2 (signal.NotifyContext reused), D3 (time.LoadLocation guarded by !*once not deleted), D4 (single construction path), D5 (exit 0 on completed cycle, 1 on whole-cycle failure); (5) no DB objects touched (no migration, no sqlc); (6) anti-gaming — no weakened criteria, no self-approved statuses; (7) performance-profile compliance — reads unaffected; (8) nightly path behavior-identical to before (same NewScheduler, Run, log lines, shutdown).
